title: Sprint slimming lens grooming notebook
body:
Purpose and context:

Quick working notebook for Sprint+1 grooming. Treat as the single-threaded ‘lens’ we’ll use to prune and shape the console/tooling backlog this week. Goal: produce a 6–8 item cutlist (shippable in sprint+1) and a 2-week runway list for follow-ups. This doc is deliberately messy — live notes from triage session with PD, UX, and Eng.

Audience:
- PMs and UX designers preparing cutlist
- Eng leads evaluating feasibility and deps
- Solutions / SEs for impact signals

High-level heuristics (the ‘slimming lens’):
1) User-visible delta: prefer items that reduce cognitive load or unblock customer onboarding flows.
2) Latency-to-value: <3 weeks engineering work for a meaningful improvement.
3) Risk & telemetry: pick things we can instrument quickly. If we can’t measure it, deprioritize.
4) Cross-product leakage: deprioritize console features that require infra/runtime changes unless coupled with a clear business SLA.
5) Reuse vs one-off: favor work that provides primitives usable by multiple routes or models.

Session notes (annotated):
- Intake queue is large; many tickets are small UI copy or visibility issues. Instead of one-off fixes, propose a ‘copy sweep’ epic (RW-1456) to standardize terminology across routes. -> assign to content owner (Priya) for a 2-day pass.
- High pain: route-level cost breakdowns are confusing for users on Dedicated. Several tickets (RW-1203, RW-1789) asking for clearer bucketization. Proposal: wireframe a small toggle that collapses advanced breakdown and surfaces a single-line estimated $/1k tokens for the selected model.
- Observability: token-level tracing surfaced by SRE is high value but risky to scope. Split into: (A) trace export (backend) and (B) UX surface. Only include UX surface in sprint if trace export is already in progress.

Wireframe writeups (quick sketches, text-first):
1) Route Cost Compact Toggle (compact-first)
- Location: Route details header > right aligned action group
- Default collapsed view: show single-line summary: "Estimated cost: $0.12 / 1k tokens (gpt-4l-medium)" with a chevron to expand
- Expanded view: token breakdown bar (prompt vs completion vs cache hits), 7-day sparklines, and a link to "explain this estimate" modal
- Acceptance criteria: linked to metric RW-MET-09 (time-to-first-cost-click)

2) Intake Triggers page (micro-onboarding for integrations)
- Purpose: help platform teams map event sources to Redwood triggers without a full onboarding call
- Content blocks: connector picker, sample payload preview, quick-run test button (runs sample request against sandbox only), common-misconfig checklist
- UX flows: success toast with sample curl snippet, failure shows line-level hints (e.g., missing api_key header)
- Acceptance criteria: test-run success rate > 90% in internal QA for three connectors

Micro-cut & prioritization candidate list (scored):
- RW-1203 Route cost compact toggle — score: 8/10 (user delta 9, effort 3, measurability 8) -> candidate for sprint+1
- RW-1456 Copy sweep epic (term alignment across console) — score: 7/10 (user delta 6, effort 2, measurability 7) -> backlog quick-win
- RW-1789 Token trace UX surface (dependent on RW-2008 export) — score: 5/10 (blocked) -> defer until export starts
- RW-1624 Intake Triggers page — score: 8/10 (user delta 8, effort 5) -> candidate if we can scope to connector templates only
- RW-1999 Model-variant quick-compare modal (shows latency, cost, accuracy notes) — score: 6/10 (useful but needs data pipeline) -> keep in 2-week runway

Cutlist draft for sprint+1 (6 items target):
1) Route cost compact toggle (RW-1203) — wireframe + small backend flag + E2E test
2) Copy sweep (RW-1456) — content pass + small UI updates (bulk PR)
3) Intake Triggers MVP (connector templates only) (RW-1624-lite) — UI + sample payloads for top 3 connectors
4) Route header accessibility fixes (small a11y tickets grouped) — group and ship
5) Quick-help shell for Dedicated onboarding (small modal with steps & links) — content + link wiring
6) Telemetry: add a lightweight telemetry event (console.cost_viewed) for cost toggle interactions

Dependencies & risks:
- RW-1624-lite needs sample payloads maintained by SEs; sync with Marco for top connectors and sandbox tokens
- Telemetry event requires tagging in analytics pipeline; coordinate with observability (ticket RW-2102)
- Token tracing UX blocked until backend export RW-2008 clears security review

Jira triage guidance (practical queries and how to label):
- Query for candidate tickets: project = CONSOLE AND status in (Open, "In Grooming") AND labels in (ux, backlog) ORDER BY priority DESC, created ASC
- Labels to use: ux, grooming-ready, needs-content, effort-small, needs-api, blocked-by-security
- When to escalate to PM: any ticket that changes pricing display, or changes default routing behavior (needs legal/inventory review)

Acceptance criteria template (reuse):
- Short description (1 line)
- User problem statement (1–2 lines)
- Success metric (numeric) e.g., reduce support volume for X by 20% OR increase feature adoption by 15%
- QA checklist (happy path + 2 failure modes)
- Analytics events (names and minimal payload)
- Rollout plan (canary % and fallback)

Stakeholder heat map (quick):
- Customer Success: cares about copy sweep and Dedicated onboarding modal (high)
- SRE/Observability: cares about telemetry + tracing (high)
- Sales/SE: cares about Intake Triggers (medium-high)
- Legal/Finance: low but flags pricing display changes

Open questions (to resolve before final cutlist):
- Do we have permission to show estimated $/1k tokens for all customers? (Legal/Finance)
- Who will own the intake connector sample payloads (SE or PD)?
- Can analytics emit console.cost_viewed within current retention SLA? (Observability)

Next steps (owners + dates):
- Wireframes: Ethan -> produce Figma quick frames for Route Cost Toggle by 2026-02-03
- Copy sweep kickoff: Priya -> list of terms + draft replacements by 2026-02-05
- Connector list: Marco -> top 3 connectors and sample payloads by 2026-02-08
- Analytics event ticket: Jenna -> open RW-2102 and map event payloads by 2026-02-06
- Grooming review meeting: scheduled 2026-02-09 10:00 PT (invite: ux, eng leads, se, cs)

Notes to self/UX: keep the toggle low-friction; prefer text fallback over complex visuals for first ship. If backend people push back on implementing a new field, fall back to a generated estimate in the client using last-7-day tokens * model-cost-per-token (with clear caveat).

Loosely-related follow-ups (2-week runway):
- Model quick-compare modal (requires model catalog hooks)
- Route-level QA runner (run sample requests against pinned model variant)
- Bulk route export CSV (admin convenience)

Slack refs (for context): #console-intake thread: "pricing-summary-proposal" (Jan 18), #console-ux: "compact-toggle-sketch" (Jan 21)

Appendix: quick ASCII schematic for cost toggle states
- COLLAPSED:
| Route name | Estimated cost: $0.12 / 1k tokens | v |
- EXPANDED:
| Prompt | Completion | Cache hits | 7d sparkline | explain link |

End notes: This should remain a living doc. After the 02/09 grooming meeting, convert chosen cuts into tidy Jira tickets using the acceptance criteria template above. If anything escalates (legal or infra), move item to 2-week runway and pick the next highest-scoring item.

-- Ethan
